title: Platform Brief: SaaS GTM — Inference Value Metrics & Battlecards (2025)
author: Maya Thompson
content:
> **Archived 2025-11-03:** this page is superseded by "Platform Brief: SaaS GTM — Inference Value Metrics & Battlecards" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

Purpose: One place for SaaS-focused positioning, value metrics, competitive battlecards, pricing rules of thumb, a short customer story and a prospect security FAQ. Audience: AEs, SEs and product marketing running discovery and technical evaluations with mid-market and enterprise SaaS platform teams.

Executive positioning (one-liner)

Redwood Inference gives platform teams fast, cost-efficient, production-grade LLM inference through one API across hosted, dedicated and private deployments, so they can ship AI features without building inference infrastructure themselves.

Top 3 buyer outcomes

- Lower per-inference cost while holding sub-100ms tail latency on common interactive flows.
- Go from prototype to SLA-backed production on the same API (hosted, reserved, private).
- Reduce compliance risk with private deployment and audit-ready telemetry.

Value metrics for discovery

- Latency (P95/P99): Hosted chat P95 is typically 80–180ms for short prompts (<256 tokens); Dedicated P99 target is <250ms. Raise tail-latency SLOs and fallback routing to smaller quantized models during spikes.
- Throughput: Batching and caching typically deliver 2–6x cost savings on high-concurrency embedding jobs. Ask for QPS and average request size.
- Cost per 1k prompt tokens: Build comps per model and quantization tier; reference the customer story below for a self-host comparison.
- Availability / SLA: Hosted: 99.5% regional uptime; Dedicated: 99.95% backed by contract. Translate these into expected downtime cost for the buyer.
- Time-to-production: Hosted onboarding is usually 1–3 days; a Dedicated proof-of-concept takes 2–4 weeks for infra and capacity provisioning.

Battlecard: competitors and positioning

- Hyperscaler-managed LLM endpoints
  - Their strengths: native cloud integration and consolidated billing.
  - Our edge: more predictable latency, a broader model catalog (open models plus tuned variants) and lower unit cost from continuous batching, quantization profiles and routing policies.
  - Message: "Managed endpoints, tuned for inference economics and predictable tail latency."

- Simple hosted LLM API providers
  - Their strengths: great developer experience, fast time-to-value.
  - Our edge: comparable ergonomics plus Dedicated/Private lanes and enterprise controls (VPC, KMS, audit logs), so customers don't replatform as they grow.
  - Message: "Prototype to SLA-backed production without rewriting your integration."

- Self-hosted open-source stacks
  - Their strengths: full control, on-prem fit for regulated data.
  - Our edge: hardened runtime, autoscaling, cost controls and rollout tooling, with optional on-prem packaging and a customer-managed control plane. Lower TCO for teams that don't want to staff deep infra expertise.
  - Message: "An optimized, maintained runtime without building an infra team."

Pricing guidance (rules of thumb)

- Levers: model family, Dedicated instance SKU, quantization tier, reserved commit vs burst, embedding vs generative unit pricing.
- Proposal archetypes:
  - Hosted starter (self-serve): no commit, pay-as-you-go per token and per embedding. Good for feature proofs.
  - Dedicated entry: 6–12 month reserved capacity (monthly commit), with capacity reservation, business-hours priority support and model access. Common for mid-market customers with steady QPS.
  - Private Deployment: platform fee + per-node license + premium support and compliance bundle. For regulated or air-gapped customers.

- Illustrative scenario (SaaS search & assistant):
  - Baseline: 3M tokens/month, mostly generation (~500 tokens/session), plus 2M embeddings/month.
  - Hosted (pay-as-you-go): roughly $6,000–$9,000/month depending on model family and streaming.
  - Dedicated (reserved, 12-month commit): roughly $3,200–$5,500/month equivalent, with stronger latency SLAs.
  - Treat these as conversation starters; final proposals need pricing desk quotes.

Pitch deck outline (6 slides)

1. Problem: inference cost growth, tail latency and operational debt at scale.
2. Vision & value: one inference runtime, predictable economics, flexible deployment.
3. Product: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize.
4. Proof points: P95/P99 benchmarks, cost comparisons vs self-host and hyperscalers, customer story.
5. Security & compliance: VPC, KMS, SOC2 / ISO posture, audit logs, private deployment.
6. Commercials & next steps: archetypes, pilot offer, success criteria, timeline.

Customer story: anonymized SaaS helpdesk platform — 6-week pilot

- Situation: The customer needed an agent-assist feature with sub-200ms P95 latency; their prototype ran on a single self-hosted instance.
- Action: Started on Hosted API, added prompt caching, then moved to a Dedicated pool with quantized variants and a canary rollout with automatic fallback.
- Results: P95 latency fell from ~400ms to ~170ms; estimated per-token cost dropped ~40% vs the self-hosted baseline.

Security FAQ for prospects

Q: Can Redwood run in my VPC / on-prem?
A: Yes, via Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) or the on-prem package for air-gapped environments. Lead time is typically 4–8 weeks depending on network and hardware; ask sales for the deployment checklist.

Q: How is data protected in Hosted?
A: TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest. Per-customer KMS keying is optional (BYOK on Dedicated & Private). Only transient inference artifacts are retained by default; retention is configurable.

Q: Do you have third-party attestations?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence, available to enterprise customers under NDA.

Q: How are audit logs surfaced?
A: Redwood Console shows request-level telemetry, per-token cost, model version and an admin audit trail; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.

Q: How do you prevent data leakage through model updates?
A: The model-onboarding team gates all updates; we issue signed model-change notices and run canary/evals against your suites. Private customers keep model binaries under their own control.

Q: How do you handle incident response and notifications?
A: A documented incident process and dedicated SRE on-call rotation. Dedicated and Private customers get a designated technical account lead (TAL) and a post-incident report within 5 business days for Sev1 incidents.

Objection handling

- "We can build this ourselves": probe hiring/retention cost for ops talent, time-to-first-SLA and ongoing tuning; offer a TCO comparison and pilot.
- "Data must stay on-prem": lead with Private deployment, checklist and timelines.
- "Hyperscaler pricing is cheaper": get real usage patterns and run a model-by-model comparison; stress tail latency and tooling burden.

Pilot success criteria and checklist

- Agreed criteria: target P95, acceptable per-token cost delta, error rate threshold (<0.5% request errors), SDK + tracing integration.
- Deliverables: sample prompts, 1–3 days of traffic replay, quality eval prompts, production routing plan, SLO definition.
- Typical timeline:
  - Week 0: kickoff, secret exchange, prompt set.
  - Week 1–2: Hosted pilot, instrumentation, tuning.
  - Week 3–4: Dedicated provisioning if needed, canary.
  - Week 4–6: stabilization and handoff.

Appendix: artifacts for deal folders

- Security pack: SOC2 evidence, data flow diagrams, private deployment checklist.
- Demo scripts: chat + embedding replay with a small staging dataset.
